components.css: .ds-search{display:grid;gap:7px;color:#101a29;font-family:'Trebuchet MS',Arial,sans-serif}.ds-search label{font-size:13px;font-weight:800}.ds-search input,.ds-search button{min-height:44px;border:1px solid #d8cfbf;border-radius:8px;background:#fffdf7;color:#101a29}.ds-search input{padding:8px 10px;font:400 16px 'Trebuchet MS',Arial,sans-serif}.ds-search p{margin:0;color:#596675;font-size:12px}.ds-search button{display:grid;gap:3px;padding:11px 12px;text-align:left;cursor:pointer}.ds-search button:hover{border-color:#9fa9b4;background:#f0eadf}.ds-search button:active{background:#ebe3d6}.ds-search input:focus-visible,.ds-search button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #2767e9;outline-offset:2px}.ds-search span,.ds-search small{color:#596675}

components.name: Administrator Navigation
components.description: Four persistent tools with a moving navy indicator; transparent button hovers keep the slide visually continuous.
components.css: .ds-nav{position:relative;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:4px;padding:5px;border:1px solid #d8cfbf;border-radius:12px;background:#fffdf7}.ds-nav>span{position:absolute;inset:5px auto 5px 5px;width:calc((100% - 13px)/4);border-radius:8px;background:#101a29;transition:transform 380ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)}.ds-nav button{position:relative;z-index:1;min-height:44px;padding:8px 12px;border:0;border-radius:8px;background:transparent;color:#596675;font:800 13px 'Trebuchet MS',Arial,sans-serif;cursor:pointer}.ds-nav button:hover{background:transparent;color:#101a29}.ds-nav button:active{background:transparent}.ds-nav button.is-active{color:#fffdf7}.ds-nav button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #2767e9;outline-offset:1px}

components.name: Public Pilot Action
components.description: A sharper public-page action that may carry cinematic lamplight while operational buttons remain navy and factual.
components.html: Bring Streetlight to your church

narrative.overview: Streetlight moves from cinematic darkness into warm daylight: a literal expression of the church bringing light to streets that may otherwise be forgotten. The public experience may be atmospheric and editorial, while the administrator workspace remains calm, map-first, and operational. Both surfaces share the same navy, cream, amber, logo, and deliberate restraint.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper against deep navy ink.
Restrained amber light, with map colors reserved for real coverage meaning.
Editorial Georgia display type paired with sturdy Trebuchet interface type.
Map-first layouts, compact controls, and clear recovery states.
Gentle depth and motion that clarify layers without making the tool feel glossy.

rules.name: The Factual Color Rule
rules.body: On maps, blue, green, amber, orange, red, and gray retain their established data meanings. Decorative styling must not borrow those colors in ways that confuse coverage state.

rules.name: The Rare Light Rule
rules.body: Amber is most effective when scarce. Use it for atmosphere and emphasis, not every button or heading.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Georgia speaks the mission; Trebuchet runs the work. Do not introduce a third font or use display type for dense controls.

rules.name: The Map Owns the Room Rule
rules.body: Tool chrome explains and edits the map; it never visually outweighs it.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A shadow signals a real layer or state. Static cards use borders and surface color instead.

dos: Do keep the map visible while administrators move through Coverage, Generate, Reconcile, and Territory.
Do use church-specific language such as tracts and outreach.
Do keep all interactive targets at least 44px and preserve visible keyboard focus.
Do make failures recoverable and keep the last valid territory or batch visible.
Do let the public page carry more atmosphere than the workspace so the two surfaces feel related without importing its cinematic density.
donts: Don't add generic SaaS gradients, glass cards, oversized metric dashboards, or decorative charts.
Don't use map-state colors as decoration.
Don't hide the normal workflow behind a wizard, hamburger menu, or AI-style recommendation.
Don't fill empty space with explanatory copy the administrator does not need.
Don't add religious ornament merely for atmosphere; the lamp, language, and purpose carry the church identity.
